answerable_part: This data can show recorded motorist deaths per 1,000 police-reported crashes in NYC, but not risk per mile driven.
metric: Annual sum of number_of_motorist_killed divided by the number of police-reported crash rows, multiplied by 1,000.
denominator: All police-reported crash rows dated in the same calendar year; 1,000 crash rows as the displayed scale.
population: All police-reported motor vehicle crash records in NYC whose crash_date is in 2013-2025; numerator sums recorded motorist deaths and denominator counts these rows.
filters: Include crash_date from 2013-01-01 through 2025-12-31 inclusive; no other filters.

data_check_meaning_and_decisions.population_rows: 2,132,218 crash records are dated in 2013-2025. Annual denominator counts are in check_2.csv.
data_check_meaning_and_decisions.date: Within the planned population there are no missing dates and no 1970-01-01 date default; DATE cannot contain empty strings or textual unknowns. Each year has an observed first date of January 1 and last date of December 31, so no endpoint year is partial by its observed date span. This does not verify that every in-year date or crash is captured. Keep all eligible date rows; exclude records outside the years by plan definition.
data_check_meaning_and_decisions.number_of_motorist_killed: 0 of 2,132,218 planned rows are missing this field; the typed INTEGER cannot contain empty strings or textual unknowns. Keep all planned rows in the numerator; no outcome rows are dropped or reclassified for missingness.
data_check_meaning_and_decisions.change: The year range was retained after the check because 2013 and 2025 both span their full calendar dates in the file.

limitations: This is recorded deaths per reported crash, not risk per mile or per journey. The data has no miles-driven exposure, and annual crash-row denominators vary substantially; min/max dates establish full calendar spans but do not establish complete capture of every crash or date.
